sense: the space between two places or things

terms.gloss: distance, space; a stretch of road or time
evidence: Caes. B.G. 1.43.1: aequum ferē spatium … aberat
Ov. M. 8.794: viae spatium, the length of the way (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Room, space, and so the distance between two points; also a span of time (spatium vītae). Latin often says how far with the verb abesse and an accusative or ablative of the distance: mīlia passuum tria abest (see away, and how far).

terms.gloss: the distance between, an interval; a gap in time
terms.comment: Properly the space between two palisades (inter vallōs); the gap between things in a row, and between moments. From a distance: ex intervallō (Liv.).

phrases.latin: Hic locus aequum ferē spatium ā castrīs Ariovistī et Caesaris aberat.
phrases.english: This place was about the same distance from the camps of Ariovistus and of Caesar.

phrases.latin: Item equitēs Ariovistī parī intervallō cōnstitērunt.
phrases.english: Ariovistus’ horsemen likewise halted at the same distance.

intervallum.html: Lewis & Short marks neither vallum nor intervallum, and de Vaan (s.v. vallum) reconstructs *walso- without ruling on the vowel. The loci collection prints intervāllō in Liv. 22.12.8; the length is not settled here.
